# Test: gyms drop minerals on kill

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic gym tests that fail while the gyms do not drop minerals, pinning the behaviour the gym-wiring task must deliver.

## Required coverage

- Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row (via the shared destruction path and via the EXPLODE button) increases the live mineral count by exactly one at the asteroid's position.
- A large/medium asteroid splits into its children without a direct mineral drop.
- No double drop: a single destruction produces exactly one drop (not one per path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the gym drop behaviour; `npm test` for the gym suites passes.
- Tests assert the drop position and count, not merely that the count increased, and are deterministic (seeded RNG).
- Tests fail before the gym-wiring task lands and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`

# Shared player-control step across all scenes

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 1 & 11).

## Summary

The sequence *input → tick weapon timers → apply P5 speed/fire-rate multipliers → physics → auto-fire* is re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` and `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, and `GymPlayer.update` inlines the scheme→input mapping instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput`. Extract one `_tickPlayer(dt)` (and keep `_readPlayerInput`) in `CombatCoreScene` so every scene advances the player identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene` owns a single `_tickPlayer(dt)` that performs, in the same order every frame: `tickWeaponTimers`, live `setSpeedMultiplier`/`setFireRateMultiplier` from the effects registry, `_readPlayerInput`→`setInput`, `physicsTick`, and `_autoFire`. `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` call it instead of their local copy. Verified by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymPlayer` consumes the shared input mapping (calls `_readPlayerInput` or an extracted shared input helper) and no longer inlines the `fourDirHandler`/`asteroidsHandler` branch. Verified by a source guard and by `GymPlayer.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3** — Timed-weapon expiry, P5 multipliers and auto-fire ordering are identical in the game and every gym for the same input and `dt`. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test booting `PlayScene` and a gym, applying a P5 effect and asserting the same speed/fire-rate outcome.
- [ ] **AC4** — `GymPowerUpsCombat` no longer uses a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the player path; the player is advanced from the supplied `dt` (the enemy-clock fix is child #2).
- [ ] **AC5** — All existing scene suites pass unchanged; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard covers `_tickPlayer`.
- [ ] **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4.
- [ ] **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — new shared `_tickPlayer(dt)`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — consume the shared step.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ8 (from epic):** should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper.*

## Plan — changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `/skill:plan AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0`: autoplan pre-check returned `decision: skip` (placeholder effort Extra Small / risk Low). Planning auto-completed via the six automated review stages. No child items were created: the parent epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` already decomposed register gaps 1 & 11 into this leaf task, and its ACs contain the test/verification obligations. No blocking clarifications were required; clarifications and one flagged AC wording issue are recorded below.

## Plan — automated review summary

Retained as a leaf task for direct implementation (measurable ACs + minimal implementation sketch):

- **Requirements & AC alignment:** AC1–AC7 trace to epic gaps 1 (player-control step duplicated) and 11 (`GymPlayer` not on the shared control core). AC1 names four consumers; AC2 covers `GymPlayer`; AC4 covers `GymPowerUpsCombat`; together they cover every consumer named in the summary. OQ8 is answered by AC2.
- **Completeness:** `## Acceptance Criteria` is present and the `## Key Files` paths are syntactically valid; all 11 referenced files exist at HEAD (`7bfe98f`).
- **Sequencing & dependencies:** no children. This item is the prerequisite (epic child #1) for boss integration (child #6) and the parity guard (child #10). Tests are embedded in AC1–AC5, so the test-first intent is satisfied without separate children.
- **Scope sizing:** one focused refactor (add `_tickPlayer`, migrate six scenes, tests, docs) — a deliverable increment.
- **Acceptance & testability:** all ACs are pass/fail; AC3 (cross-scene equivalence) and AC5 (duplicate-body guard) name automated verification.
- **Polish & handoff:** description is actionable; the Key Files list matches the consumer set.
- **AC coverage review:** `run_coverage_review` returned `recommendation: proceed` (leaf item; no children).

## Plan — clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: "OQ8 — should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal?" Answer (epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`): *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.* Final accepted: **yes** — AC2 requires `GymPlayer` to consume the shared input mapping.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the sequence described in the summary actually one identical sequence in every named scene?" Research (HEAD `7bfe98f`; read of `PlayScene.tick` L557–572, `GymFormationScene.tick` L1299–1318, `GymWeapons.tick` L178–195, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` L154–170, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick` L258–275): the scenes run **subsets with different ordering**, not identical copies — `PlayScene` runs tickWeaponTimers → multipliers → `_handleTeleport` → input → physics → auto-fire; `GymFormationScene` runs timers → multipliers → input → physics → auto-fire with teleport later; `GymWeapons` omits the P5 multipliers; `GymPowerUpsUtility` omits tickWeaponTimers and auto-fire; `GymPowerUpsCombat` omits timers, multipliers and auto-fire. Resolution (epic assumption, "the shipped game is canonical"): the shared `_tickPlayer(dt)` runs the full ordered sequence and each gym's absent feature resolves to a no-op (multiplier 1, empty weapon list). Recorded as an implementation assumption; if a test shows a behaviour change in those gyms the difference must be recorded in the epic and approved.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does `GymPowerUpsCombat` use a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the *player* path (AC4)?" Research: the only fixed 16 ms step is `_nextFireTime += 16` inside `_tickScouts` (`GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` L424), which is the **enemy-fire** clock and belongs to epic child #2 (`AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46`, "Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock"); the player path already advances from the supplied `dt`. **OPEN QUESTION (AC4 wording):** AC4 should be read as "the `GymPowerUpsCombat` player path uses the supplied `dt`" (already true); the 16 ms enemy clock is fixed by child #2, not by this item. Intent is clear enough to implement; the wording is flagged for correction rather than rewritten here (rewriting could change intent).

**OQ-NOTE (effort/risk):** the autoplan pre-check generated a zeroed placeholder estimate (O=M=P=0, 0.00 h → Extra Small / Low) because `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` submits a fixed `{o:0,m:0,p:0}` payload. Treat the `effort`/`risk` fields as a placeholder; `<WIP-id>` should receive a genuine `/skill:effort-and-risk` estimate before implementation is dispatched.

# Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge

## Problem statement

Replace the game's hand-rolled procedural Web Audio synthesis (~2,253 lines in `src/audio/effects.ts`) with **ToneForge** (`../ToneForge`) — build-time rendered WAV assets consumed via Phaser. All SFX are produced through one dedicated audio toolchain, ensuring reproducible, seed-deterministic output.

## Decision: Baked assets (approach A)

**Chosen approach: Build-time baked WAV assets.** ToneForge CLI renders each cue to a WAV file during a build step, consumed by Phaser at runtime. This matches ToneForge's documented game-dev workflow, keeps the browser dependency surface clean (no Node-only deps leaking into the game bundle), and is the simplest integration path.

**Trade-off:** Runtime variation (pitch jitter, thrust-driven hum) is lost in baked form. These are handled separately:
- Thruster hum: baked multiple variants or played via a lightweight Tone.js shim at runtime (to be evaluated in a follow-up work item).
- Pitch jitter: baked multiple variants with different seeds to approximate variation.

**Child work items created:**
- Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible) — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`
- Consider switching to runtime generation when possible — child work item here
- Update ToneForge license to MIT — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`

## Users

- **Game developer (primary):** Wants a single, well-documented audio toolchain with deterministic output, easy recipe authoring, and reproducible builds.

### User stories

- As the game's developer, I want every SFX cue produced via ToneForge so that audio is authored, generated and varied reproducibly with one toolchain.
- As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.
- As the game's developer, I want to author new recipes in ToneForge without modifying game audio code.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Approach recorded:** Baked assets (A) approach is chosen with rationale; any required ToneForge changes are split into child work items (runtime-awareness, license update, future runtime consideration).
2. **Cue-to-recipe mapping:** Every cue exported by `src/audio/effects.ts` today is mapped to a ToneForge recipe/stack/sequence (existing or newly authored) or explicitly retired, documented on this item.
3. **Recipes in ToneForge:** Any newly authored recipes/presets live in `../ToneForge` and are documented there (name, character, seed).
4. **Audible character preserved:** The audible character of each retained cue matches GDD §7.3 (waveform family, frequency contour and nominal volume preserved within audible similarity).
5. **Global volume/mute:** `setSfxVolume`/`setSfxMuted` continues to affect all cues; SettingsScene controls still work.
6. **Single shared context:** Exactly one shared `AudioContext` is created; a new scene/cue does not construct a second context (invariant asserted in tests).
7. **No-op when unavailable:** In an environment without an `AudioContext`, every cue degrades to a no-op and never throws (verified by headless tests).
8. **Advance cues ≥ 500 ms:** Advance cues remain ≥ 500 ms and cue→fire scheduling remains gap-free where required.
9. **Deterministic build:** Rendering is seed-deterministic, checksums are recorded, and the generation step is reproducible in CI.
10. **Pinned dependency:** ToneForge is consumed reproducibly (`file:` dependency to sibling checkout, pinned to a commit or tag); the build must not silently depend on an unpinned checkout.
11. **No Node-only deps in browser:** Node-only ToneForge dependencies do not leak into the browser game bundle.
12. **Tests and build pass:** Full test suite passes (`npm test`), and `npm run build` / `npm run typecheck` pass clean.
13. **Documentation updated:** GDD §7.3, the audio-directory tree note and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` describe the ToneForge-based pipeline.

## Constraints

- GDD §7.3 currently mandates "zero external audio assets" — the baked approach changes this stance; the GDD must be updated to reflect build-time generation.
- ToneForge is v0.1.0; API may change. Pin to a specific commit/tag.
- ToneForge license must be resolved (MIT — child work item in sibling repo).
- Build-time generation must be reproducible (deterministic seeds, checksums).
- The thruster hum is continuous and thrust-driven — may need a runtime shim or multiple baked variants.

## Existing state

- ~2,253 lines of procedural Web Audio in `src/audio/effects.ts`
- Consumers import cue functions directly from `../audio/effects`
- ToneForge sibling checkout at `../ToneForge` (commit `c48fed5`, MIT license — TBD in repo)
- ToneForge CLI: `toneforge`/`tf`, commands include `generate`, `show`, `list recipes`, `sequence`, `stack`, `explore`, `play`
- Recipe catalogue is card-game oriented; only `weapon-laser-zap` is game-action relevant

## Desired change

- Build pipeline step renders all game cues to WAV via ToneForge CLI
- Phaser plays WAV files instead of procedural synthesis
- New recipes/presets authored in ToneForge for game cues
- SettingsScene volume/mute controls wired to Phaser audio node
- Tests updated to assert ToneForge-based behaviour

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Replace procedural synthesis with Phaser audio playback
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Update tests for ToneForge-based cues
- `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — Update master tests
- `../ToneForge/src/recipes/` — Add game recipe definitions
- `../ToneForge/presets/` — Add game presets
- `scripts/build-audio.sh` (new) — Build step to render WAVs via ToneForge CLI
- `public/audio/sfx/` (new directory) — Baked WAV assets
- `package.json` — Add `file:` dependency on ToneForge
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — Update audio direction
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Update per-enemy audio

## Related work

- Child work items: ToneForge runtime-awareness, ToneForge license update, future runtime consideration
- References: GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction), ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md
- ToneForge sibling repo: `../ToneForge`

# Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice)

## Problem statement

When a run ends, `PlayScene` cuts straight to `GameOverScene`, which renders
identical content for both outcomes — the only difference is a two-word title
(`VICTORY` in green vs `DEFEAT` in red). Victory has no fanfare and no
celebration, and the loss screen gives no distinctive visual or audible signal
that the run is over. The two most consequential moments in the game therefore
feel flat and interchangeable.

## Users

- As a player who has beaten the Central AI boss, I want a triumphant finale
  (fanfare + visual celebration) so that winning feels rewarded.
- As a player who has lost the run, I want a clear, sombre visual and audible
  signal so that defeat feels consequential and is instantly distinguishable
  from victory.
- As a player entering my initials on the game-over screen, I want the
  celebration/defeat treatment to run behind the UI without blocking or
  delaying my keyboard or pointer input.

Example user stories:

- *"I finally beat the boss and the game just… ended. I want it to feel like a
  win — music, sparks, confetti, the lot."*
- *"When I lose I barely notice; the screen looks the same as a win. I want a
  clear 'you lost' moment."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Victory fanfare (audio).** On a run ending in victory (`won: true`) a
   dedicated procedural cue `playVictoryFanfareSound()` plays: a rising major
   arpeggio (≥ 3 distinct notes) resolving into a sustained chord, total
   ~1.5–2.5 s, with a light sparkle/crackle tail. It routes through the master
   SFX gain (so mute/volume apply), peaks at volume ≤ 0.2, and is a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext`. A unit test asserts the scheduled node topology
   and no-throw behaviour headless.
2. **Victory celebration (visual).** A shared module `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`
   exposes `spawnVictoryJuice(...)`, composing at least three layers — a
   celebration particle/confetti burst, one or more expanding shockwave
   ring(s), and a bright flash/glow — all tunable via exported constants with
   per-layer `ENABLE_*` toggles (mirroring `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`). The
   celebration is rendered on `GameOverScene` (victory branch) as a sustained
   treatment behind the score/initials/leaderboard UI. A test asserts the
   layers are created and cleaned up.
3. **Defeat signal (audio + visual).** On defeat (`won: false`)
   `playDefeatStingSound()` plays a descending, sombre cue that is distinct
   from both the victory fanfare and the existing `playPlayerDestructionSound()`,
   and `GameOverScene` renders a distinct defeat treatment (e.g. red vignette
   plus a desaturation/glitch flicker) that appears only on the defeat branch.
   A test asserts defeat-only objects/cues are present for `won: false` and
   absent for `won: true`.
4. **Non-blocking, lifecycle-safe, graceful.** The treatments never intercept,
   delay or block keyboard/pointer input on `GameOverScene` — initials entry
   and Return to Menu remain fully usable throughout. Every juice display
   object is tracked in a scene-owned registry destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (no
   leaks across scene restart). The defeat treatment layers on top of the
   existing in-run *fatal* death juice (`spawnPlayerDeathJuice`) without
   replacing or weakening it. All new cues are safe no-ops without an
   `AudioContext`.
5. **Parity and documentation.** Any behaviour shared with scene paths that can
   reach a run end is implemented once and consumed by both (per the
   AGENTS.md gym↔game parity convention); where a gym has no run-end screen,
   the reason is documented. `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.2 (visual
   style / juice) and §7.3 (SFX catalogue + Player Audio Character) are updated
   with the new victory/defeat treatment and cue entries, and new tunables are
   documented in code comments.
6. **Tests and full suite.** Unit tests cover victory/defeat audio synthesis
   (node topology, volume ceiling, safe no-op headless), juice composition and
   teardown, outcome-branch rendering, and non-blocking input. `GameOverScene.test.ts`
   is extended. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Procedural Web Audio only, zero external audio assets** (GDD §7.3); the
  new cues follow the existing `src/audio/effects.ts` synthesis style.
- **No background music** — background music is explicitly out of MVP scope
  (GDD §7.3). The victory treatment is SFX + VFX only.
- **Player cue volume ceiling ≤ 0.2**, routed through the master SFX gain so
  the Settings mute and volume controls apply.
- **Safe no-op without an `AudioContext`** (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
  browsers) — audio must never be a hard dependency.
- **Non-blocking**: the treatment is cosmetic only and must not delay or
  interfere with leaderboard/initials input. Gameplay, scoring and leaderboard
  behaviour are unchanged.
- **Canvas/palette**: 960×540 near-black palette (GDD §7.1) — cyan/green for
  victory, red/desaturated for defeat.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- **Browser autoplay policy** (GDD §6.7): `GameOverScene` is only reached after
  the player has interacted (Start/Play), so the `AudioContext` is already
  unlocked; no new unlock path is required.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._finishRun(won)` calls `scene.start('GameOverScene', { won, score })`.
  Victory is triggered from `_damageBoss()` (boss destroyed) → `_finishRun(true)`;
  defeat from `_loseLife()` when lives reach zero → `_finishRun(false)`.
- On the fatal defeat path, `spawnPlayerDeathJuice(this, x, y, 'fatal', …)` and
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()` already fire *before* the transition
  (`src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts`), but the scene switch stops `PlayScene`
  almost immediately, so the GameOver screen carries no lasting treatment.
- `GameOverScene` (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`) renders a black rectangle, a
  coloured `VICTORY`/`DEFEAT` title, the final score, optional initials entry,
  the leaderboard, and Return to Menu — otherwise identical for both outcomes.
- No victory-specific audio or VFX exists anywhere; `src/audio/effects.ts` has
  no victory/defeat cue.
- Juice precedent: `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` and `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`
  use a pure `resolve*Params()` + exported tunables + per-layer `ENABLE_*`
  toggles + a caller-owned effects registry cleared on `SHUTDOWN`.
- Audio precedent: every cue in `src/audio/effects.ts` routes through
  `ensureMasterGain(ctx)` and degrades to a no-op without an `AudioContext`.

## Desired change

- Add two procedural cues to `src/audio/effects.ts`:
  - `playVictoryFanfareSound()` — rising major arpeggio + sustained chord +
    sparkle tail.
  - `playDefeatStingSound()` — descending sombre sting (+ optional filtered
    noise tail), distinct from the hull-breach cue.
  Both exported with `VICTORY_*` / `DEFEAT_*` tunable constants, volume ≤ 0.2.
- Add a shared end-of-run juice module `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` with a pure
  `resolveEndOfRunJuiceParams(outcome)` mapping and `spawnVictoryJuice(...)`
  (plus the defeat screen treatment) built from layered, individually
  switchable effects.
- Trigger the victory fanfare at the moment of the win in `PlayScene`, and
  render the sustained celebration on `GameOverScene`'s victory branch so it
  remains visible for the whole screen without introducing a long blocking
  delay before the transition.
- Render the defeat treatment and play the defeat sting on `GameOverScene`'s
  defeat branch, layered on top of the existing in-run fatal death juice.
- Keep the treatment behind the existing UI; wire all juice objects into a
  registry cleaned up on `SHUTDOWN`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` — **New**: shared victory/defeat juice composition,
  pure params resolver, tunables, per-layer toggles and effect registry.
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.test.ts` — **New**: unit tests for params, layer
  composition and teardown.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — **Edit**: add `playVictoryFanfareSound()` /
  `playDefeatStingSound()` and their exported constants.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — **Edit**: tests for the new cues (topology,
  volume ceiling, no-throw headless).
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — **Edit**: render victory/defeat treatment
  behind the UI; trigger the defeat sting; own and clear the effect registry.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: outcome-branch rendering,
  teardown and non-blocking-input tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit**: trigger the victory fanfare/celebration
  at the moment of the win.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: §7.2 (juice) and §7.3 (SFX
  catalogue / Player Audio Character); §4.5/§5.1 only if flow notes change.

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Motion/flash discomfort* — flashes, glitch flicker and particles can be
  uncomfortable. Mitigation: keep layers short, reuse the existing tunable
  patterns, keep per-layer `ENABLE_*` toggles; a reduce-motion accessibility
  option is a separate (linked) work item, not part of this scope.
- *Scene-transition timing* — existing tests assume `GameOverScene` is active
  ~350 ms after boss defeat (`PlayScene.test.ts`), so a long in-run hold would
  break them. Mitigation: compose the *sustained* celebration on
  `GameOverScene` (no long blocking delay); keep any in-run flourish short and
  update timing-sensitive tests deliberately.
- *Audio overlap / clipping* — the fanfare must not drown other cues or clip.
  Mitigation: ≤ 0.2 peak, single one-shot through the master gain.
- *Parity convention* — `GameOverScene` is currently only reached from
  `PlayScene`; gyms have no run-end screen. Mitigation: keep the shared helper
  in `src/vfx/`, document the justified absence of a gym consumer, and run the
  parity/docs assertions.
- *Scope creep* — "loads of juice" could expand into background music, a
  cutscene or a leaderboard redesign. Mitigation: keep to SFX + VFX + screen
  treatment; capture extras as linked work items, not scope.
- *Pre-existing flaky test* — AH-0MUINWNPI000G6MU (boss victory → return to
  menu) fails under full-suite parallel load; not caused by this work, but the
  suite must be green before finishing.

**Assumptions** (producer-validatable)

- *Victory* means `won: true` (the boss was defeated); *defeat* means
  `won: false`. There is no other run-end path.
- No background music is added (GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope).
- The treatment is purely cosmetic: score, lives, leaderboard and initials
  entry are unchanged.
- The primary consumer is `PlayScene` → `GameOverScene`; gyms do not reach a
  run-end screen, so no gym behaviour change is required (documented).

## Related work

See the automated "Related work (automated report)" section below (added by the
`find-related` skill).

- Need juice when the player is destroyed (AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY) — *completed*;
  provides the in-run fatal death juice this work layers on top of and must
  stay visually distinct from.
- Phase shift needs to be auto-applied when needed (AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8) —
  *completed*; precedent for a dedicated cue + screen overlay that was

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fanfare/juice live?** Options: (A) both an in-run
  flourish and a persistent `GameOverScene` treatment; (B) in-run only;
  (C) `GameOverScene` only.

  celebrating while the player enters initials. The agent's recommended option

  heavy flashes to defeat too.

# Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit

## Goal

Produce the authoritative cue-to-recipe mapping for the ToneForge migration (parent epic AC2) and decide the disposition of every exported cue in `src/audio/effects.ts` — mapped to an existing ToneForge recipe, scheduled for new recipe authoring, or explicitly retired.

As the game's developer, I want every SFX cue accounted for before authoring work starts, so nothing silently disappears in the migration.

## Scope

- Enumerate every exported function in `src/audio/effects.ts` (~50 cues) plus `blip`, `explosionPitchFactor`, `updateThrusterSound` and `stopThrusterSound`.
- For each cue record: current synthesis summary (waveform, contour, nominal volume), GDD §7.3 reference, production consumers in `src/`, and disposition:
  - `existing-recipe` — map to an existing ToneForge recipe (e.g. `weapon-laser-zap`).
  - `new-recipe` — needs authoring; record the proposed slug, character and target seed range.
  - `retired` — no production consumer and no gameplay value.
- Confirm or deny the unused-cue candidates already identified in planning:
  - `playWeaponChangeSound()` — no production consumer, no test reference.
  - `playMajorExplosionSound()` — only referenced by tests; GDD §7.3 states it is "retained but unused by the timeout path".

- Record the final mapping table as a comment on this work item and cross-link it from the parent epic.

- Every exported cue in `src/audio/effects.ts` has exactly one disposition (`existing-recipe`, `new-recipe`, or `retired`) recorded in the mapping table.
- Each `existing-recipe` row names the ToneForge recipe and justifies the audible-character match.

# Author game-specific ToneForge recipes

## Goal

Author the game-specific recipes identified by the cue-to-recipe mapping task in the ToneForge sibling repository (`../ToneForge`), so every non-retired game cue has a deterministic, seed-documented recipe that can be rendered to WAV.

As the game's developer, I want to author new recipes in ToneForge without modifying game audio code.

## Scope

- Add one parameter module per recipe under `../ToneForge/src/recipes/` (e.g. `game-thruster-hum-params.ts`) exporting a seed-derived params interface and getter.
- Register each recipe in `../ToneForge/src/recipes/index.ts` with a deterministic duration and offline graph builder.

- For composite cues (e.g. player death = thump + body + shrapnel hiss), compose via a stack/sequence/preset under `../ToneForge/presets/` or `../ToneForge/stacks/` rather than duplicating synthesis.

- Composite cues are composed from existing primitives where possible; any new primitive is itself covered by a recipe test.

# Deterministic WAV build pipeline

## Goal

Create a build step that renders every game recipe to baked WAV assets under `public/audio/sfx/` via the ToneForge CLI, with recorded checksums, so the game bundle is self-contained and the generation step is reproducible in CI.

As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.

## Scope

- Add `scripts/build-audio.sh` that iterates the game recipe manifest, invokes `tf generate --recipe <slug> --seed <n> --output public/audio/sfx/<name>.wav`, and fails fast on any render error.
- Emit `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` (SHA-256 per asset) after a successful render.
- Add an `npm run build-audio` script and wire it into `npm run build` as a preceding step.
- Add a reproducibility check: re-rendering with the same seeds must reproduce identical checksums; drift fails the script.
- Add a CI step that runs `npm run build-audio` and fails if generated assets differ from the committed checksums.
- Handle pitch-jitter variants (explosions) by rendering a small fixed set of seeds and selecting among them at runtime.
- Thruster hum is out of scope for baking (handled by the runtime shim task).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run build-audio` renders all manifest recipes to `public/audio/sfx/` and exits non-zero on any failure.
- `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` records a SHA-256 for every rendered asset.
- Re-running `npm run build-audio` with unchanged seeds produces an identical `checksums.json`.
- `npm run build` invokes the audio build before the Vite bundle step.
- CI fails when a rendered asset's checksum does not match the committed manifest.
- The script's recipe manifest is a single source of truth consumed by both the build and the tests.
- No Node-only ToneForge dependency is bundled into the browser output (verified by build inspection).

## Dependencies

- Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (must exist before they can be rendered).

## Deliverables

- `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Recipe manifest file consumed by the script.
- `public/audio/sfx/` baked WAV assets plus `checksums.json`.
- `package.json` `build-audio` script and `build` wiring.
- CI job step invoking the build and verifying checksums.

## Key Files

- `scripts/build-audio.sh` — new build script.
- `package.json` — `build-audio` and `build` scripts.
- `public/audio/sfx/` — baked asset output directory.
- `../ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js` — `tf`/`toneforge` CLI entry point.

# Audio playback contract tests

## Goal

Write the failing contract tests that define the ToneForge/Phaser audio playback behaviour before the implementation rewrite, so the rewritten `src/audio/effects.ts` is driven by executable requirements.

As the game's developer, I want the audio contract pinned by tests before the rewrite, so the migration cannot silently drop a cue or break headless operation.

## Scope

- Tests must be written first (TDD) against the preserved public API of `src/audio/effects.ts`; they are expected to fail until the rewrite task lands.
- Contract areas:
  - **Cue coverage:** every non-retired cue in the mapping table has a callable export that does not throw.
  - **No-op degradation:** with no `AudioContext` (headless), every cue returns without throwing.
  - **Single context:** exactly one `AudioContext` is created across repeated cue calls and scene initialisation (invariant assertion).
  - **Volume/mute:** `setSfxVolume`/`setSfxMuted` affect all cues, including live-updating currently playing sounds; mute restores the prior volume on unmute.
  - **Advance cues:** advance cues have a duration ≥ 500 ms and cue→fire scheduling is gap-free where required.
  - **Asset mapping:** each cue maps to the expected baked asset key (or shim for the thruster hum).
- Use a mock/no-op audio provider so the suite runs headlessly and deterministically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Contract tests exist for every area above and are run by `npm test`.
- The no-op test proves every cue is safe without an `AudioContext`.
- The single-context test fails if a second `AudioContext` is constructed.
- Volume/mute tests assert both initial and live-update behaviour.
- Advance-cue tests assert duration ≥ 500 ms and gap-free scheduling.
- The tests are deterministic and do not depend on real audio hardware.
- All contract tests pass once the rewrite task is complete.

## Dependencies

- Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit (fixes the cue set under test).

## Deliverables

- Updated `src/audio/effects.test.ts` contract suite.
- Updated `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` for master volume/mute and advance-cue scheduling.
- A reusable headless audio test double.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — module under contract.

# Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback

## Goal

Replace the ~2,253 lines of procedural Web Audio synthesis in `src/audio/effects.ts` with Phaser playback of the baked ToneForge WAV assets, preserving every retained public cue function signature so consumers do not change.

As the game's developer, I want Phaser to play WAV files instead of procedural synthesis, so all SFX come from the one ToneForge toolchain.

## Scope

- Keep the exported API stable: cue names, `setSfxVolume`, `setSfxMuted`, `updateThrusterSound`, `stopThrusterSound`, `playVolumeFeedback`, and the `_*ForTests` helpers.
- Route playback through Phaser's audio system (`this.sound` / a scene-injected sound provider) rather than constructing per-cue `AudioContext`s.
- Keep exactly one shared audio context; assert the invariant is maintained.
- Degrade to a safe no-op when no audio context/Phaser sound manager is available (headless tests, autoplay-blocked browsers).
- Preserve advance-cue timing and gap-free cue→fire scheduling.
- Wire `SettingsScene` volume/mute to the Phaser audio node.
- Remove the procedural synthesis code once behaviour is covered by the contract tests.

- Every retained cue export has the same signature as before the rewrite.
- Cues play the baked asset recorded in the mapping table (or delegate the thruster hum to the shim).

- Exactly one `AudioContext` is created across the whole game lifecycle (contract test passes).
- Every cue is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (contract test passes).

# Thruster hum Tone.js shim

## Goal

Implement the continuous, thrust-driven thruster hum as a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim, since baked WAV variants cannot reproduce a pitch/gain-continuous, thrust-coupled loop.

As the game's developer, I want the thruster hum to remain continuous and thrust-driven, so the tuning slider stays audible and the hum stays in lockstep with the flame animation.

## Scope

- Add a small Tone.js-based runtime shim that owns only the thruster hum; all other cues are baked assets (decision recorded on the parent epic).
- Preserve the existing `updateThrusterSound(level)` / `stopThrusterSound()` contract consumed by `Player.preUpdate`.
- Reproduce the documented character: triangle fundamental ~60 Hz + sine undertone ~35 Hz + band-pass filtered noise (700–1100 Hz) whoosh, gain ≤ 0.075.
- Mirror the flame growth/shrink timing (30 ms growth, ~4x decay) and avoid clicks on retrigger.
- Stop cleanly on release, respawn, player destroy and scene shutdown so no audio nodes leak.
- Degrade to a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- Add Tone.js as a pinned runtime dependency and verify it is the only new browser runtime dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The thruster hum is continuous while thrust is held and stops cleanly on release/respawn/destroy/scene shutdown.
- Hum gain tracks `getEngineSoundLevel` and stays ≤ 0.075.
- No clicks on retrigger; growth/decay match the documented flame timing.
- The shim is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- No audio nodes leak after repeated thrust start/stop cycles (asserted in tests).
- Tone.js is pinned and is the only new browser runtime dependency introduced.
- `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

## Dependencies

- Audio playback contract tests.
- Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback.

## Deliverables

- Thruster hum shim module.
- Wiring from `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` to the shim.
- Shim tests covering continuous gain tracking, clean stop and no-op degradation.

# Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene

## Goal

Consume ToneForge reproducibly and ensure no Node-only dependency leaks into the browser game bundle, satisfying the parent epic's pinned-dependency and clean-bundle acceptance criteria.

As the game's developer, I want a reproducible, pinned audio toolchain so builds never silently depend on an unpinned sibling checkout.

## Scope

- Add the ToneForge dependency to the game `package.json` (build-time CLI consumption via `file:` to the sibling checkout, or a git reference pinned to a commit/tag).
- Pin to the resolved commit/tag and record it; the build must not silently depend on a floating checkout.
- Verify the browser bundle contains no Node-only ToneForge modules (`node-web-audio-api`, filesystem/CLI code).
- Add a bundle-hygiene assertion or CI check that fails if a Node-only module is imported into the browser entry graph.
- Confirm the ToneForge licence work (sibling work item) is resolved or tracked as a blocker.
- Record the pinned revision in the build script or a lockfile-adjacent manifest.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `package.json` declares a reproducible ToneForge dependency pinned to a commit or tag (not a floating branch).
- The resolved pinned revision is recorded and referenced by the build.
- The browser bundle contains no Node-only ToneForge module (verified by build inspection).
- An automated check fails if a Node-only module enters the browser entry graph.
- The build succeeds without requiring an unpinned `../ToneForge` checkout beyond the declared dependency.
- The ToneForge licence status is resolved or explicitly recorded as an open blocker.
- `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Planning Complete — ToneForge audio migration

Decomposed the epic into **8 implementation features** plus the **3 pre-existing sibling children** (Runtime-awareness, runtime evaluation, licence update). Plan follows test-first ordering and vertical-slice phasing.

### Created children

| # | Work item | Type | Priority | Depends on |
|---|-----------|------|----------|-----------|
| C1 | Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit (AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT) | task | high | — |
| C2 | Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51) | feature | high | C1 |
| C3 | Deterministic WAV build pipeline (AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD) | feature | high | C2 |
| C4 | Audio playback contract tests (AH-0MUTYV8RJ009MWKJ) | task | high | C1 |
| C5 | Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback (AH-0MUTYV92Y000WJ8Z) | feature | high | C3, C4 |
| C6 | Thruster hum Tone.js shim (AH-0MUTYV9ES003A3HJ) | feature | medium | C4, C5 |
| C7 | Update audio documentation (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT) | docs | medium | C1, C2 |
| C8 | Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene (AH-0MUTYVA2C000SNPO) | chore | high | C5 |

### Vertical-slice phasing

- **Phase 1 — recipe + asset pipeline:** C1 → C2 → C3 (cue catalogue → recipes → deterministic WAVs).
- **Phase 2 — playback:** C4 (tests first) → C5 (rewrite) → C6 (thruster shim).
- **Phase 3 — hardening:** C7 (docs), C8 (pinning + bundle hygiene).

Every phase cuts through code, tests, docs and build/CI. Between phases, re-read and update the next item's description before starting it.

### Parent AC → child traceability (manual)

The `tree_coverage` helper reports `proceed` but parses **0 parent ACs** because the parent uses a numbered list; the helper only recognises `- `/`+ ` bullets. Coverage was therefore verified manually:

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|-----------|-----------|
| 1. Approach recorded | C1 + existing AH-0MUTVP8600019HFO / AH-0MUTVQDH2008DEF6 / AH-0MUTVVAL1002AY12 |
| 2. Cue-to-recipe mapping | C1 |
| 3. Recipes in ToneForge | C2 |
| 4. Audible character preserved | C2, C5, C6 |
| 5. Global volume/mute | C5 |
| 6. Single shared context | C4, C5 |
| 7. No-op when unavailable | C4, C5, C6 |
| 8. Advance cues ≥ 500 ms | C4, C5 |
| 9. Deterministic build | C3 |
| 10. Pinned dependency | C8 |
| 11. No Node-only deps in browser | C8 |
| 12. Tests and build pass | C4, C5, C6, C8 |
| 13. Documentation updated | C7 |

### Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should thruster hum use baked variants (multiple WAV files played randomly) or a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim?" Answer (operator): **shim** — lightweight Tone.js runtime shim. Final: shim. Effect: C6 created as its own child; C3 explicitly excludes the thruster hum from baking; AC4/AC7 handled across C2/C5/C6. Prior planning had left this open ("to be evaluated in a follow-up work item").
- Q: "Should the build script run as a pre-build step (before `vite build`) or as a separate `npm run build-audio` command?" Answer (operator): **separate command run as part of the build**. Final: `npm run build-audio` invoked by `npm run build`. Effect: reflected in C3 ACs.
- Q: "Are there any cues in the current `effects.ts` you know should be retired (unused by any scene)?" Answer (operator): **don't know**. Research (agent, consumer analysis via `rg`): `playWeaponChangeSound()` has no production or test reference; `playMajorExplosionSound()` is referenced only by tests and GDD §7.3 calls it "retained but unused by the timeout path"; `playTankDestructionSound()` has no production consumer and GDD §7.3 calls it "intentionally-unwired". Final: defer the confirm/retire decision to C1, which owns the disposition of every cue.
- Q (approval gate): "This plan requires your confirmation because its effort is Medium scale." Answer (operator): **approved**. Final: approved (in-session resume; item re-claimed via `StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed`).

### Observations / recommendations (non-blocking)
